submission.justification: Based on comprehensive simulation studies, Sensor-T2 (thin-pitch sensor with large signal sharing) at 132 μm thickness achieves the best single-hit spatial resolution of 5.702 μm, significantly outperforming Sensor-T1 (~8.76 μm at best) and Sensor-T3 (~14.2 μm at best). The thin-pitch design with large signal sharing enables superior position interpolation, which is critical for the innermost layer where tracking precision is paramount. The 132 μm thickness represents the optimal balance: thick enough to generate sufficient signal for good charge sharing, but thin enough to minimize multiple scattering and maintain excellent spatial resolution. This configuration meets all technical requirements: it is within the 50-300 μm thickness constraint, compatible with the readout chip's 50x50 μm² pixels, and qualified for bump bonding. The relatively modest thickness also benefits radiation tolerance and material budget considerations for the innermost layer of the high-luminosity tracker.

requirements.requirement: Achieve the best possible single-hit spatial resolution in the innermost layer
requirements.evidence: Sensor-T2 at 132 μm achieves 5.702 μm resolution, which is the best result among all tested configurations. This is ~35% better than Sensor-T1 (8.76 μm) and ~60% better than Sensor-T3 (14.2 μm).

requirements.requirement: The sensor must be one of the three technologies listed in candidate_specs.md
requirements.evidence: Sensor-T2 is explicitly listed in candidate_specs.md as 'thin-pitch sensor with large signal sharing' and is one of the three candidate technologies.

requirements.requirement: The sensor must be suitable for the radiation environment of the innermost layer
requirements.evidence: All three candidate sensors are stated to be 'qualified for bump bonding to the readout chip' in candidate_specs.md, implying they have been pre-qualified for the application. The 132 μm thickness is relatively thin, which helps with radiation tolerance by reducing the depletion voltage after irradiation.
The recommended thickness of 132 μm is well within the specified range of 50-300 μm.
